statement: For all positive integers n,m,t and every integer k>=2, every finite tagged-occurrence coverage family f_i(T)=sum_{u in U_i} 1[S_(i,u) intersects T] on [n], with nonempty incidence subsets and each item belonging to at most t occurrences across all functions, has a coloring chi:[n]->[k] satisfying max_{i,c,c'} |f_i(chi^{-1}(c))-f_i(chi^{-1}(c'))| <= 4kt(kt-1)^2, independent of n,m and all feature counts and sizes. Equal incidence subsets at distinct occurrences remain distinct. A deterministic polynomial-time construction exists for explicitly listed incidences and item slots, allowing binary-encoded k and t. This resolves the immutable source.md qualitative polynomial-existence question; no claim retains the sharper exponents of the source's logarithmic bound.
contribution: Proposed full-scope size-independent bound via a categorical rainbow-witness reduction: Hall matching assigns disjoint k-item witness blocks to all large occurrences; cyclic block states preserve their coverage identically, and the remaining features have class-affine coverage matrices with column l1 norm at most kt. Known multiple-choice Beck-Fiala rounding then telescopes over at most (kt-1)^2 classes. Hall matching, graph independent classes and the 2||A||_1 rounding theorem are credited prior tools, not claimed innovations. The proposed structural reduction and qualitative removal of size dependence are the submitted mathematical delta; current bounded primary comparison found no equivalent, while fresh novelty and substantive-value review remain required.
